_meta.source: book/on_the_origin_of_risk (Timlett 2025), ch. 2 (geologic map meta-model), Technical appendix I (fractional meta-models, Fig. 25-26)

data_schema.description: A set of functions, each partly implemented across the components of one solution

failure_modes: Calling a data hierarchy a meta-model and expecting it to hold domain information
Leaving fractions unmeasured, so neither their cost nor their readiness is known
gloss: A model at the level of the solution that partly implements several models at once
invariants: The domain can be read by inspecting a fractional meta-model
Full and absent implementation are the limiting cases k = n and k = 0
mechanism: Three kinds of meta-model differ in where they sit. A hierarchical meta-model goes one level up and keeps only data types and relations, so its domain cannot be read from it; a geologic map meta-model, or a neural network described as a meta-model, is of this kind. A domain-specific language goes one level down and restricts a general language to one domain. A fractional meta-model sits at the level of the solution itself and implements one model fully while implementing parts of others: k of the n components a function needs are in place. The simplest case is a {{computational_channel}}, where generated but rejected inputs are fractionally implemented functions that a change to the acceptor would complete. Full implementation is the special case k equals n.
